test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Gita bought 80 oranges at the rate of ₹9.50 per orange. She sold 25% of these at ₹12 each and one-third of the remaining at ₹10 each. At what price per orange should she sell the remaining oranges to get an overall profit of 25%?
solution:
**Given:**

Gita bought 80 oranges at the rate of ₹9.50 per orange.

She sold 25% of these at Rs12 each and one-third of the remaining at Rs10 each.

She has to make an overall profit of 25%

**Concept used:**

Profit is calculated on the cost price

**Formula used:**

Selling price = cost price + profit

Profit percentage = (Net profit / cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

The total cost price of 80 oranges is 80 × 9.5 = Rs 760

25 % of 80 = 80 × 25 /100 

⇒ 20

The selling price of 20 oranges is (20 × 12) = Rs 240 

Remaining oranges is 80 - 20 = 60

1/3 of the 60 = 60 × 1 /3

⇒ 20

So she sold the next 20 oranges at 20 × 10 = Rs 200

To make a 25% Profit overall selling price is 760 × 125 / 100 = Rs 950

She has to make a profit of 950 - (240 +200) = Rs 510 by selling the remaining (80 - 40) 

⇒ 40 oranges

So the selling price will be 510 / 40 = Rs 12.75

**She** **has to sell for Rs 12.75 to make an overall profit of 25%**
